Title: Malaysia's wage structure needs review, says council
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's wage structure needs to be reviewed to ensure that workers earning above the minimum wage also benefit from periodic salary adjustments, said the National Wages Consultative Council.
National Wages Consultative Council (MPGN) member Prof Emeritus Tan Sri Anuwar Ali said the government currently sets the minimum wage at RM1,700 per month.
However, he said there was no clear mechanism to ensure workers earning RM1,800 or RM1,900 also receive salary increments.
"This situation has caused many employers to focus solely on implementing the minimum wage without reviewing the salary structure for employees above that threshold.
"This group ends up squeezed as their income remains virtually stagnant even as the cost of living continues to rise," he said at the 2nd Malaysia Wisdom Conference 2026 here today.
Anuwar added that starting salaries for fresh graduates have shown a declining trend compared with two decades ago.
"About 20 years ago, fresh graduates with a bachelor's degree could start their careers with a salary of around RM3,500 a month.
"Today, due to an increasing number of graduates and pressures in the job market, starting salaries are nearing the minimum wage rate. In fact, some graduates only receive between RM2,000 and RM2,500 a month," he said.
He said this was a major challenge that both the federal and state governments must address to ensure a sustainable labour market.
Anuwar added that the government must ensure economic growth creates more high-quality jobs to absorb the annual influx of graduates.
"The emphasis on Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) is a good step, but it must be supported by the expansion of economic activity and job opportunities commensurate with the skills these graduates possess.
"When TVET graduates enter the job market, they will face the same issue if quality job opportunities do not expand alongside skill enhancements," he said.
Anuwar added that the government and industry players need to work together, with greater emphasis on developing local industries to expand, innovate and create more quality employment opportunities.
He said organisations such as the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers and the Malaysian Employers Federation should play a more active role in formulating industrial development strategies aligned with the objectives of the Five-Year Malaysia Plans and market demands.
"I see too much focus being placed on attracting foreign direct investment. Of course, foreign investment is important, but much of it comes due to low labour costs and involves labour-intensive industries," he said.
Anuwar said local industries must advance to higher levels through technology adoption, innovation, and productivity growth, mirroring developed nations such as South Korea.
"A major portion of our industry consists of small and medium enterprises, most of which only employ around 50 to 100 workers.
"If we look at history, in the 1960s, South Korea's development level was not much different from Malaysia's.
"Today they are far more advanced because they successfully developed competitive, technology-driven local industries," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan's Hiroshima marks 81st anniversary of atomic bombing
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's Hiroshima on Thursday marked the 81st anniversary of the United States (US) atomic bombing of the city amid growing concerns over nuclear risks and rising global tensions, reported Xinhua.
During an annual memorial ceremony held at the Peace Memorial Park in the western Japanese city, Hiroshima Mayor Kazumi Matsui delivered the Peace Declaration, highlighting the catastrophic consequences of nuclear weapons and calling for nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament through multilateral efforts.
"Downplaying the inhumanity of nuclear weapons and accepting the use of force to pursue one's own prosperity risk cycles of violent retaliation that could ultimately result in another Hiroshima or Nagasaki," the mayor warned.
As the number of atomic bombing survivors continues to decline, Matsui also called on younger generations to take the initiative and build a broad consensus toward the abolition of nuclear weapons.
A moment of silence was observed at 8.15 am local time, the exact moment when an atomic bomb dropped by a US bomber detonated over the city on Aug. 6, 1945, killing around 140,000 people by the end of that year.
Three days after the world's first-ever nuclear attack decimated Hiroshima, a second atomic bomb was dropped on Nagasaki in southwestern Japan.
As the only country in the world to have suffered atomic bombings, Japan has long upheld the Three Non-Nuclear Principles, which prohibit possessing, producing or permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons into Japanese territory.
In recent years, however, calls to revise the principles have grown in the country, especially within the ruling bloc.
Local media previously reported that the government of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was considering revising the principle prohibiting the introduction of nuclear weapons into Japan.
The reported move has sparked widespread concern among various sectors of Japanese society.
The
Tokyo Shimbun
reported on Wednesday that at least 128 local assemblies from 36 prefectures across Japan have submitted written opinions to the Diet since Takaichi took office in October last year.
The submissions urged the government to uphold the Three Non-Nuclear Principles. The figure marks a record high.

Title: Care home where man beaten to death found operating without valid licence
Article:
IPOH: A care home in Taman Choong Kwee, Tanjung Rambutan, where a 54-year-old man was beaten to death last Tuesday, was operating without a valid licence from the relevant authorities.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said preliminary investigations revealed that the care home, which has been operating since 2012, only held a business registration with the Companies Commission of Malaysia.
He said no documents had been produced to show that the premises was registered with the relevant agencies or departments.
"So far, investigations show there is no documentation indicating the premises is registered or holds a valid operating licence from the Social Welfare Department, Ipoh City Council, or an authorisation letter from the Health Ministry.
"The premises was also found to be without closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras," he said at a press conference after the rank-pinning ceremony for the Perak Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) chief and Taiping district police chief at the Perak Senior Police Officers' Mess here today.
The ceremony also saw Assistant Commissioner Mohd Ridzuan Nor Ihsan formally assume the post of Perak CCID chief after serving in the acting capacity, while Assistant Commissioner S. Saravanan was appointed Taiping district police chief.
Alwi said the victim was one of 21 residents at the private care home.
Preliminary investigations showed the incident occurred on the night of Aug 3 after the victim allegedly became aggressive and disturbed other residents.
He said a caretaker allegedly ordered the victim to be tied up before several residents, together with the caretaker, assaulted and stomped on him.
"A post-mortem conducted by a forensic specialist at Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital confirmed that the cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head.
"Following the incident, police arrested 5 men, comprising 4 residents and a caretaker, aged between 35 and 55. They have been remanded for 4 days from Aug 5 until Aug 8," he said.
Alwi said police were completing investigations from all angles, including recording statements from witnesses and working closely with the relevant agencies.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
He added that the victim's body had been claimed by his family, while investigations were ongoing, including efforts to obtain the victim's medical records.
"Appropriate action will be taken against the operator or management of the care home if any other violations of the law are discovered," he said.
Yesterday, Alwi confirmed the arrest of 5 people, including a caretaker, following the death of a male resident at the care home in Tanjung Rambutan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Theta Edge shares hit six-month high on RM3bil Penang LRT contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of Theta Edge Bhd climbed to a six-month high after the company secured a RM3.028 billion railway systems contract for the Penang Light Rail Transit (LRT) Mutiara Line through a joint venture.
The stock opened five sen, or 9.09 per cent, higher at 60 sen before surging as much as 17.5 sen, or 31.82 per cent, to 72.5 sen, its highest since Jan 22.
By the midday break, the counter eased to 69 sen, still up 14 sen, or 25.45 per cent, with 5.96 million shares traded. It was the stock's busiest trading day since Oct 10, 2024, with volume exceeding 10 times its 200-day moving average.
Today's rise marked Theta Edge's biggest single-day gain since Nov 28, 2025, when the stock surged after reporting stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings.
At 69 sen, the company had a market capitalisation of RM81.4 million. Year-to-date, the stock remained down four sen, or 5.48 per cent.
Theta Edge, through its 10 per cent-owned joint venture with Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd (MRCB), has secured the RM3.028 billion system turnkey contract for the Penang Mutiara Line LRT project.
MRCB owns the remaining 90 per cent stake in the joint venture.
The contract, awarded by Mass Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp), is a key milestone in the delivery of Penang's first metro rail system, allowing railway systems design and integration to proceed in parallel with ongoing civil works.
The joint venture has been appointed turnkey contractor for the engineering, procurement, design, construction, testing, commissioning and maintenance of the railway systems under Package STC.
The scope includes the delivery of electric trains, depot equipment, signalling and train control systems, trackwork, power supply and distribution systems, and maintenance vehicles.
It also covers telecommunications and information technology systems, ticketing systems, automatic platform gates, the railway supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system, and a computerised maintenance management system.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, Theta Edge said it will undertake selected technology-related work packages covering railway systems, telecommunications and digital infrastructure.
The detailed allocation of work packages will be finalised under the joint venture agreement.
MRCB is one of Malaysia's largest infrastructure and property developers, with an established track record in rail construction and transit-oriented developments.
It is best known for developing KL Sentral, the country's largest integrated transport hub, and has undertaken major rail infrastructure works for the MRT Sungai Buloh-Kajang Line and the LRT3 Shah Alam Line.
MRT Corp said the 29km Mutiara Line remains on track for completion by December 2031 as construction gathers pace.
To date, 45 pile caps and 32 pier columns have been completed, while works are underway across 14 of the 19 sections under Civil Main Contract 1, covering the alignment from Silicon Island to Komtar.
Land acquisition for the first civil works package has reached 93 per cent, while the tender evaluation for Civil Main Contract 2, covering the extension from Komtar to Penang Sentral, is ongoing and is expected to be awarded in November.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Q2 growth "should be okay": Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic growth for the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026) "should be okay", Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said ahead of the official 2Q gross domestic product (GDP) announcement on Aug 14.
Responding to reporters after delivering his keynote address at the RHB Progress Series 2026 today, Amir Hamzah, however, did not elaborate further.
Bank Negara Malaysia is scheduled to announce Malaysia's Q2 GDP data next week, which will provide a clearer picture of the country's economic performance during the April-June period.
The Statistics Department released its advance GDP estimates for Q2 2026 on July 17, which stated that Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.8 per cent, following the preceding quarter's growth of 5.4 per cent.
The performance was supported by growth in almost all economic sectors other than agriculture, which contracted, it said.
Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.4 per cent in 1Q 2026, surpassing the advance estimate of 5.3 per cent. Robust domestic demand, investment activities and exports continue to drive growth.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five senior officers promoted to key KL police leadership post
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Five senior police officers have been promoted and appointed to key leadership positions within the Kuala Lumpur police contingent as part of efforts to strengthen command and operations.
Senior Assistant Commissioner (SAC) Sazalee Adam has been appointed the new Kuala Lumpur Criminal Investigation Department (CID) chief, replacing SAC Zulkarnain Samsudin, who has been appointed Selangor CID chief.
Sazalee, the former Dang Wangi district police chief, was among five officers promoted from Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) to SAC rank.
The other officers promoted are former Sentul district police chief Basri Sagoni, former Kuala Lumpur CID deputy chief (Intelligence/Operations) Zulkarnain, former Kuala Lumpur Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) chief Haslah Bachok, and Kamaruzaman Md Alib.
Basri has been appointed head of the D7 Prevention/Detention/Surveillance Division at CID Bukit Aman, while Haslah will serve as principal assistant director (Intelligence/Operations) at the Standard Compliance Division of the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department, Bukit Aman.
Meanwhile, Assistant Commissioner Kee Hang Kee has taken over as Kuala Lumpur NCID chief from Haslah, while Assistant Commissioner Saefuddin @ Mohd Fitri Abdul Rahman has been appointed deputy chief of the Kuala Lumpur Special Branch (Intelligence/Operations).
Superintendent Nuzulan Mohd Din has succeeded Sazalee as Dang Wangi district police chief, while Superintendent Jasni Zolpa has replaced Basri as Sentul district police chief.
The rank-pinning and handing-over ceremony was held at the Kuala Lumpur police contingent headquarters today and witnessed by Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus.
Speaking after the ceremony, Fadil said each promotion reflected recognition of an officer's performance and dedication, while also carrying greater responsibility to uphold integrity and professionalism.
"The ceremony also reflects the continuity of leadership within the police.
"Transfers are an important process to ensure the organisation continues to grow with fresh ideas, experience and approaches without affecting the continuity of service delivery to the public," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five charged in Sabah over false Perkeso Daya Kerjaya 2.0 claims
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Four company owners and a marketing executive were separately charged today with submitting false documents linked to incentive claims under the Social Security Organisation's (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Programme.
All five pleaded not guilty before Special Corruption Sessions Court Judge Andi Razalijaya A. Dadi.
The accused are Pausia Abu, 49; Arzeanti Jafar, 40; Nur Farhanah Jamil, 38; Mohd Azhar Ramali, 39; and marketing executive Foo Fong Kent, 31.
Foo faces three charges, while Pausia and Azhar each face two charges. Arzeanti and Nur Farhanah each face one charge.
According to the charges, the accused allegedly submitted Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Verification Forms in the names of their respective companies to a Perkeso agent, despite having reason to believe the documents contained false material particulars intended to mislead the principal.
Foo was alleged to have committed the offences between May 30 and Oct 9 last year at Infinity Profit Enterprise in Warisan Square, Jalan Tun Fuad Stephens, here.
Pausia, the owner of Hajah Yanong Enterprise, was accused of committing the offences on March 15 and 18, 2024, at Kilang SME Bank, Jalan Papar.
Azhar, owner of Cyber Vision Enterprise, was alleged to have committed the offences on June 7 and Aug 14, 2024, at premises in Alamesra Plaza Utama, Jalan UMS.
Arzeanti, owner of Tasek Emas Enterprise, was accused of committing the offence on Aug 6, 2024, at Desa Sri Taman Laya-Laya, Tuaran, while Nur Farhanah, owner of Afijay Bersatu, was alleged to have committed the offence on Aug 19, 2024, at Jalan Tuaran By-Pass, Manggatal.
All five were charged under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, punishable under Section 24(2) of the same Act.
Upon conviction, they face imprisonment of up to 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the false material particulars, where such particulars can be valued or involve money, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
The court fixed Sept 14 for case management and granted bail to all accused with two local sureties.
Foo was granted bail of RM10,000 with a RM7,000 deposit, while Pausia and Azhar were each granted bail of RM10,000 with a RM5,000 deposit.
Arzeanti was granted bail of RM8,000 with a RM4,000 deposit, while Nur Farhanah was granted bail of RM8,000 with a RM3,500 deposit.
The court also ordered all accused to report to the nearest MACC office once a month, surrender their international passports, and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses before or during trial.
Separate trial dates were fixed for each accused, with Arzeanti's trial set for Oct 12 to 16, Foo's from Oct 19 to 23, Pausia's from Oct 12 to 14, Azhar's on Oct 19 and Oct 21 to 23, and Nur Farhanah's from Oct 26 to 30.
The prosecution was conducted by MACC prosecuting officer Norsham Baharom.
Foo was represented by counsel Lim Chun Yuan, while Pausia, Arzeanti and Mohd Azhar were represented by counsel Sylvester Kuan. Nur Farhanah was unrepresented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KTMB: No timeline yet for reopening Kulai-Kempas Baru line
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Electric Train Service (ETS) operations between Kulai and Kempas Baru remain disrupted today as repair works continue following an accident that damaged the overhead electrification system.
Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said there is still no timeline for the reopening of the affected section as crews continue removing a fallen concrete parapet that struck the overhead line equipment on both the northbound and southbound tracks.
"The recovery effort was delayed after the lorry company, Transmare-Chemie (M) Sdn Bhd, informed KTMB at 3am that a 120-tonne crane required to remove the concrete structure had yet to be secured.
"The company was expected to provide an update on the availability of the crane this morning, with lifting operations projected to begin at 10am if the equipment became available.
"However, the reopening of the line will depend on the progress of the removal works, technical inspections and safety clearance," KTMB said in a statement today.
Operations and technical personnel remain at the site to coordinate recovery efforts and ensure all safety requirements are met before services resume.
Three morning ETS departures from JB Sentral have been affected.
Passengers travelling on ETS 9442 to Padang Besar, ETS 9524 to KL Sentral and ETS 9326 to Butterworth are being transported by shuttle buses to Kulai Station before continuing their journeys by train.
Meanwhile, Shuttle Selatan services between Pasir Gudang and JB Sentral continue to operate, while shuttle services between Kulai and Kempas Baru remain suspended until further notice.
KTMB said the temporary travel arrangements would remain in place until inspections and repair works are completed and the line is certified safe for operations.
Affected passengers who choose not to continue their journeys are entitled to full refunds, while assistance is available from KTMB personnel at the stations.
The rail operator said updates on the recovery works and train operations would be announced through its official channels and apologised for the inconvenience caused.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: About 20,000 residents hit by foul odour, black water in Iskandar Puteri
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: About 20,000 residents living near the SILC Industrial Area here have been grappling with foul odours and black-coloured water for years, with allegations that irresponsible factories have been discharging industrial waste into a monsoon drain.
The pollution, affecting several housing estates along Jalan SILC 2/4, has raised fears of a public health and environmental crisis, with residents claiming the black, sludge-filled water eventually flows into Sungai Pulai and nearby rivers.
Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad warned that failure to address the issue promptly could trigger a disaster similar to the
2019 Sungai Kim Kim
toxic pollution incident.
"The pollution is not only affecting the nearly 20,000 residents from four housing areas but also factory workers and school communities in the vicinity.
"What is even more worrying is that if this issue is not properly addressed, we could see a repeat of the Sungai Kim Kim incident here," he told the 'New Straits Times' today.
Pandak visited the site after receiving complaints from residents to assess the situation first-hand.
He said residents claimed they had repeatedly lodged complaints with the relevant authorities, but alleged that while investigations had been carried out, enforcement action had failed to resolve the issue.
"I personally experienced nausea and vomiting after spending time at the site yesterday and had to seek treatment at a clinic after the inspection," he said.
Pandak said firm action must be taken against those responsible if investigations uncover breaches of environmental laws or licence conditions.
He urged the Iskandar Puteri City Council, the environment department and the state health department to carry out a comprehensive investigation to identify the source of the pollution and prevent further contamination.
Meanwhile, Johor Environment Department director Dr Mohd Famey Yusoff confirmed that a complaint was lodged and investigations are underway.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tong Herr trading halted pending announcement, volume hits four-year high
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Trading in the shares of Tong Herr Resources Bhd was suspended this afternoon pending a material announcement by the company.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the trading halt took effect at 12.16pm. It did not disclose the nature of the forthcoming announcement.
Prior to the suspension, Tong Herr's shares rose 5.56 per cent or 10 sen to RM1.90, with 236,000 units changing hands, a level not seen since May 2022.
At RM1.90, the Penang-based company's market capitalisation stood at RM299.12 million. The counter has gained nearly 37 per cent, or 51 sen, so far this year.
Headquartered in the Perai Free Industrial Zone, Tong Herr is listed on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia under the industrial products and services sector.
The group manufactures and sells stainless steel fasteners, including nuts, bolts, screws and other threaded products, as well as aluminium extrusion and related products through operations in Malaysia and Thailand.
Its products are used in industries including solar energy, petrochemicals, machinery assembly, telecommunications and construction, according to its website.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Warisan KL launches Xplorasi Warisan to rediscover Kuala Lumpur
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Warisan KL and its strategic partners will host Xplorasi Warisan KL: Edisi Merdeka on Aug 30, 2026, inviting Malaysians to rediscover Kuala Lumpur's heritage through a citywide adventure celebrating the spirit of independence.
The heritage-based exploration will take participants through Kuala Lumpur's historic core, combining teamwork, discovery and interactive challenges across key landmarks within the Warisan KL heritage corridor.
More than a race, the event aims to retrace Malaysia's journey to nationhood, beginning at Stadium Merdeka, where independence was declared in 1957, before concluding at Dataran Merdeka, the site where the national flag was first raised.
Along the route, participants will uncover stories of heritage, resilience and nation-building while engaging in heritage-themed missions, puzzles, photo challenges, stamp collections and digital activities designed to bring the city's history to life.
The explorace will take place alongside wider Merdeka celebrations at Warisan KL landmarks, including activities at Stadium Merdeka in the Merdeka 118 precinct and Ambang Merdeka festivities at Dataran Merdeka.
Warisan KL said the initiative reflects its people-centred approach to heritage preservation by transforming historic sites into vibrant spaces for learning, discovery and community engagement.
Through partnerships involving government agencies, private sector organisations, cultural practitioners and local communities, Warisan KL aims to preserve and promote Kuala Lumpur's heritage while encouraging greater public participation.
The event is open to families, students, corporate teams, heritage enthusiasts, content creators and tourists. Participants will end their journey at Dataran Merdeka, joining the Ambang Merdeka celebrations featuring cultural performances, bazaars, entertainment showcases and countdown activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four charged with submitting false documents for Daya Kerjaya 2.0 claims
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Four business owners were charged in the Sessions Court here today with a total of 30 counts of submitting false documents in Daya Kerjaya 2.0 incentive claims.
Phua Ai Ling, 45, Wong Joon Hong, 40, Goh Chee Wai, 43, and
Neoh Wooi Lee, 50, pleaded not guilty to separate charges before Judge Irwan Suainbon.
They were separately charged under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 for allegedly submitting documents containing false particulars in support of claims under the Daya Kerjaya 2.0 programme.
The Daya Kerjaya 2.0 programme provided employers with a monthly RM1,500 wage incentive over six months for each eligible worker hired, including persons with disabilities, former prisoners and senior citizens.
According to the charges, the offences were allegedly committed between March 1 and Aug 26, 2024, involving several companies and applications submitted under the employment incentive programme.
Phua, the owner of Great Solutions Management, was charged with one count involving a worker verification form submitted on July 31, 2024.
Wong, the owner of JH Food Court, faced two charges allegedly committed on Aug 26, 2024.
Goh, who was linked to Tojeda Enterprise Sdn Bhd, claimed trial to six charges involving multiple applications allegedly submitted between March 1 and April 15, 2024.
Neoh, meanwhile, faced 21 charges involving four different companies. The alleged offences were committed between April 10 and Aug 26, 2024.
Deputy Public Prosecutors
Nurnajihatul Idayu Mohd Azuyar and Lim Jin Hong prosecuted. Wong and Neoh were represented by counsel K Mahendran while Goh was represented by Teh See Khoon. Phua was unrepresented.
Nurnajihatul Idayu asked the court to set bail at RM12,000 each for Phua and Wong while Lim asked the court to set bail at RM12,000 for Goh and RM48,000 for Neoh.
Nurnajihatul Idayu and Lim also sought additional conditions requiring the accused to report to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office once a month, surrender their passports to the court and refrain from coming in contact with the victims and prosecution witnesses.
"Your Honour, for the purpose of bail, I believe the primary factor that should be taken into consideration is the seriousness of the offence in this case.
"This is an offence charged under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act and should be distinguished from ordinary criminal offences.
"The prosecution is offering bail of RM12,000 for this charge against the accused. In addition, the prosecution seeks several additional bail conditions," she told the court.
Mahendran, Teh and Phua appealed for minimal bail.
Phua appealed to the court to consider her current financial situation.
"My business is in a very difficult state because of changes in the market and the decline in demand. My business has suffered badly and I have incurred losses on many occasions.
"I also have to care for my father, who has Stage 4 cancer. He requires substantial funds for his treatment at any time.
"I give my assurance to the court that I will report to the MACC office every month as required. I respectfully ask the court to reduce my bail to RM5,000 so that I can manage my financial difficulties.
"I also ask the court not to require me to surrender my passport because I hope to take my 78-year-old father overseas for treatment.
"This is our last hope of bringing him abroad," Phua said.
Mahendran and Teh appealed for lower bail, citing financial hardship, medical conditions and family responsibilities.
Mahendran told the court that up until today, Wong had cooperated fully with MACC officers and even attended court this morning as required.

Title: 19-year-old college student faces murder charge over stabbed newborn
Article:
KLUANG: A 19-year-old female college student will be charged in the Magistrate's Court here tomorrow with the murder of her newborn baby.
The infant's body with multiple stab wounds was found in a toilet bowl at a house in Taman Setia Mutiara last month.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said the decision was made after investigation papers were referred to the Johor deputy public prosecutor's office.
He said the prosecution had directed that the teenager be charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
"Based on the directive, the 19-year-old student will be charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code for allegedly murdering her newborn baby," he said in a statement today.
Bahrin said the suspect's 19-year-old boyfriend was released and would testify as a prosecution witness during the trial.
Police had earlier arrested the couple to assist investigations into the death of a
newborn baby girl
at a house where they had been staying.
The arrests followed a police report after the female student was admitted to the Enche Besar Hajjah Kalsom Hospital.
The case came to light after the student was taken to the hospital by a teacher after complaining of severe stomach pains.
Medical examinations later revealed that she had recently delivered a baby. Doctors also found that she had another baby still in her womb.
Earlier investigations also found that the suspect's boyfriend admitted to giving her RM450 in an attempt to induce a miscarriage.
Initial examinations on the deceased newborn revealed several stab wounds on the body. However, the cause of death is yet to be determined.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang Education Dept vows protection for student in cyberbullying case
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Education Department has assured protection for a student allegedly targeted in a sexual harassment and cyberbullying case that is currently under police investigation.
In a statement today, the department said it was giving its full cooperation to police to facilitate investigations.
It said an internal investigation was also being carried out to examine all aspects related to the incident.
"The department's main focus at this time is to protect the student who is the victim.
"Psychosocial support interventions are being carried out to assist the affected student," it said.
The department said it would not compromise on any form of sexual misconduct or bullying, adding that stern action would be taken against any individual found guilty.
Yesterday, a
46-year-old mother urged authorities to expedite investigations
into those allegedly responsible for repeatedly targeting her 17-year-old daughter through sexual cyberbullying.
The woman, who wished to be known only as Nur, said her daughter, an SPM candidate, had suffered emotional distress after her face, name, class and phone number were allegedly circulated through obscene posters and fake social media accounts since April.
She said her daughter had been left emotionally traumatised, often crying and feeling too embarrassed to attend school after her face was allegedly edited onto nude images.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Penang police for comments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Britons take drastic measures including sleeping in kitchen to cope with heat
Article:
LONDON: One in six Britons are taking "drastic action" including sleeping in the kitchen, missing work or booking hotels, to cope with heatwaves, Citizens Advice has found, reported PA Media/dpa.
The charity said millions across the United Kingdom (UK) are "trapped in homes they can't cool," with almost half (44 per cent) saying they lack basic control over keeping their homes from overheating.
It is demanding government action on a "now year-round crisis" of "soaring heat in summer and unaffordable energy bills in winter."
Action taken by those struggling to cope included sleeping in unconventional places like the kitchen, garden, or on a balcony, taking sick days, unpaid leave or annual leave, or paying for hotels.
A further four million said they had to use makeshift solutions like taping tin foil, cardboard, or damp sheets to windows.
The study found poorly designed homes, which act like "heat traps," and the high cost of cooling equipment such as air conditioning were making people feel helpless against the hot weather.
Half (51 per cent) of tenants – including those who rent privately and those in social housing – felt they lack the basic control needed to stop their homes overheating, compared with 40 per cent of homeowners, the poll found.
The study also found 90,000 heat network consumers were unable to turn off their central heating even in summer.
Citizens Advice chief executive Dame Clare Moriarty said: "For far too many people, a summer heatwave doesn't mean enjoying the sun – it means being trapped in a sweltering home with no control over the temperature."
"We're now facing a year-round crisis, where poorly designed housing stock is acting as a giant heat trap in summer and as an ice box in winter."
"The Government has a vital opportunity to help fix this through the Warm Homes Plan.
"By investing in better insulation, ventilation, and heat network upgrades, we can ensure people's homes are warmer in the winter and safer and cooler in the summer."
A government spokesman said: "We are changing the rules so that for the first time ever people can access grants for air-to-air heat pumps, which can cool as well as heat homes."
"We are already taking action to strengthen protections for tenants experiencing dangerous overheating and ensuring new residential buildings are designed to minimise unwanted heat from the sun."
Yonder, a UK polling and research company, surveyed 2,105 UK adults on July 1-2.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PJ MP claims constituency funds routed through PKR division chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung has claimed that public funds allocated to the constituency are being channelled through a PKR division chief.
Lee, whose access to the federal government's MyKhas portal was revoked in May, made the claim in a Facebook post today.
He shared a screenshot of a WhatsApp group message in which a PKR division chief purportedly informed members that applications for Petaling Jaya constituency funds could now be referred to him.
The New Straits Times is withholding the division chief's name pending a response.
"Parliamentary allocations are public funds meant for the benefit of all citizens, not to be managed by any political party office-bearer," Lee said.
He said he had sought an explanation through formal channels but received no response, prompting him to raise the matter publicly.
Lee called on the government to clarify whether the funds remained under Putrajaya's control or were being administered through PKR, saying transparency was necessary to avoid the perception that public allocations had been turned into party funds.
"Are other MPs whose MyKhas access has been blocked experiencing the same situation, where their constituency allocations are channelled to ruling party leaders in their respective areas?" he asked.
The MyKhas access of the MPs for Subang and Ampang has also been blocked.
Lee also called on the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission to clarify whether such a disbursement mechanism complied with established governance, integrity and legal requirements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Toyo Tyre donates RM30k to Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Toyo Tyre Sales and Marketing Malaysia Sdn Bhd has launched its Community Prihatin Toyo initiative with a RM30,000 contribution to the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund, reinforcing its commitment to community welfare alongside business growth.
The mock cheque was presented by Toyo Tyre Sales and Marketing Malaysia Sdn Bhd president and managing director, Tan Song Chye, to Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund representative Muhammad Nazim Ismail.
The donation is part of the company's broader corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives, which provide financial assistance to underprivileged Malaysians requiring life-saving medical treatment and surgery, while also supporting other vulnerable groups.
Speaking at the launch, Tan said the initiative embodied the spirit of Malaysia Prihatin and reflected the company's belief that success should be measured not only by business growth but also by its positive impact on society.
"True success is not measured solely by sales or technology.
"It is measured by our impact on the community.
"As we take this step forward, we remain grounded in our responsibility to give back," he said.
Tan added that the initiative also reflects the company's newly unveiled brand identity, Buatan Malaysia, Keunggulan Jepun ("Made in Malaysia, Japanese Excellence"), which combines Malaysian manufacturing excellence with Japanese engineering standards.
As of the 2026 financial year, the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund has helped 143 underprivileged Malaysians gain access to essential medical treatment.
Media Prima expressed its appreciation to Toyo Tyre for supporting the fund's humanitarian mission, which relies on public and corporate contributions to continue assisting those in need.
Members of the public who wish to contribute to the fund may do so via Bank Muamalat account 1401 0008 8427 18.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor's call for more health workers is about service, not politics – Health Exco
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor rejected claims that its repeated calls for the federal government to urgently fill vacancies in state public hospitals were politically motivated.
State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the appeal was solely aimed at ensuring better healthcare services for the people.
"Johor had consistently backed its appeals with financial commitments and practical measures to strengthen the state's healthcare system instead of merely highlighting shortcomings.
"The state government had spent RM65 million to upgrade healthcare facilities, fund locum doctors at major hospitals, implement decanting projects for maternal and child health clinics, and roll out other healthcare initiatives," he said in a statement today.
Yesterday, Dr Rafidah Abdullah, a public health physician and prominent healthcare advocate urged Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi to go beyond calling on the Health Ministry whenever hospitals face staff shortages.
She said meaningful reforms should include abolishing the contract appointment system, restoring pension schemes, and improving salaries, allowances and benefits for healthcare workers.
She took to her Facebook, saying proactive measures would address the workforce shortage more effectively than appeals alone.
She had described calls without accompanying policy solutions as "theatre."
The medical practitioner, who served the Health Ministry for more than 28 years, said the manpower shortage was a longstanding issue that should already be well understood by a second-term menteri besar.
Ling said Johor had taken numerous proactive measures, including allocating RM5.825 million for pantry assistance to hospitals and health clinics, RM2.8 million in special Hari Raya aid for healthcare workers, and RM14.18 million under Bantuan Kasih Johor for healthcare civil servants.
He said claims that Johor is politicising this issue are unfounded.
Responding to Dr Rafidah's remarks, Ling said Johor had repeatedly raised the staffing shortage with the Health Ministry, the Public Service Department and the federal government since 2023, including at meetings of the menteri besar and chief ministers as well as during a series of engagements with the health minister.
He said Pasir Gudang Hospital still had 1,192 vacancies out of 2,271 approved posts despite the facility being completed, while Sultanah Aminah Hospital was short of 613 personnel; and Sultan Ismail Hospital had 285 vacant positions.
"As long as these vacancies remain unfilled, doctors, nurses and other healthcare personnel will continue working long hours, shouldering heavier workloads and facing a higher risk of burnout," he said.
Ling said Johor was not seeking to blame any party but wanted earlier commitments to be translated into concrete action so that the people could receive more efficient and higher-quality healthcare services.
On Tuesday, Onn Hafiz said that the Pasir Gudang Hospital, despite being equipped with modern facilities and specialist services, was still
unable
to operate

Title: Former PH Rantau candidate, wife charged over unregistered clinic operation
Article:
SEREMBAN: A former Pakatan Harapan candidate for the Rantau seat in the recent Negri Sembilan election was charged at the Sessions Court today with operating an unregistered medical clinic.
Dr Azizul Hakim Mahdi, 35, was charged together with his wife, Noor Ameera Rahmat, 35, and their company before Judge Shahrul Rizal Majid.
All the accused pleaded not guilty.
According to the first charge, the company was found to have operated a private medical clinic without registration under Section 27 of the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998.
The company was charged under Section 4(1), which carries a maximum fine of RM500,000 upon conviction.
For the second charge, the couple, in their capacity as company directors, were accused of jointly operating a private medical clinic without registration under Section 27 of the same Act.
The charge, framed under Section 4(1) of the same Act and punishable under Section 5(2)(aa) read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, carries a fine of up to RM300,000, imprisonment of up to six years, or both, upon conviction.
The offences were allegedly committed at a premises in Taman Bandar Senawang here at around 11.30am on July 8.
The next mention date was fixed on Sept 17.
Dr Haslina Zamani represented the prosecution and the accused were represented by lawyer Muhammad Abdul Fateh Mohd Rahmat.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New BMW iX3 heralds Neue Klasse era in Malaysia, priced at RM378,800
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The new BMW iX3 50 xDrive M Sport Pro has been unveiled in Malaysia, marking the debut of the brand's Neue Klasse electric vehicle (EV) portfolio here.
The fully electric sports activity vehicle (SAV) comes with a recommended retail price of RM378,800.
It is the first Neue Klasse model to arrive in the country and has been recognised as the 2026 World Car of the Year and World Electric Vehicle of the Year.
BMW Group Malaysia managing director Benjamin Nagel said the new iX3 represents the brand's most significant technological leap in a generation.
He said the model introduces BMW's future direction for premium vehicles while redefining the driving experience in the segment.
The iX3 features BMW's sixth-generation eDrive technology based on an 800-volt architecture, delivering 345 kilowatt (kW) of power.
It generates 645 Nm of torque through a dual-motor all-wheel-drive system, powered by a 108.7 kWh battery.
The vehicle offers a driving range of up to 805 km under the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) standard with DC fast charging of up to 400 kW support, allowing up to 372 km of range to be added in 10 minutes.
BMW has also introduced a completely redesigned exterior for the iX3 compared with previous models, featuring a bold new visual identity.
The design includes a vertically positioned illuminated kidney grille, slim front and rear lighting units, flush door handles and sculpted body panels.
It is also equipped with 22-inch Y-Spoke M bi-colour alloy wheels paired with red M Sport brake calipers.
Inside, the cabin adopts a minimalist layout centred around BMW's new panoramic iDrive system and digital interface.
The interior features a 43.3-inch windscreen-wide display, a 17.9-inch central touchscreen and BMW Operating System X.
The system includes an enhanced artificial intelligence-powered intelligent personal assistant for a more connected driving experience.
Standard equipment includes electrically adjustable M Sport seats with memory, heating and massage functions, alongside a heated steering wheel.
Other features include a Harman Kardon 13-speaker sound system, wireless charging, three-zone automatic climate control and a panoramic glass roof.
Rear passengers receive adjustable seat backs, dedicated climate controls and USB-C charging ports for added convenience.
The iX3 provides 520 litres of luggage capacity, expandable to 1,750 litres when the rear seats are folded.
It also comes with a 58-litre front storage compartment located beneath the bonnet for additional practicality.
Safety and driver assistance features include driving assistant plus and parking assistant professional with remote parking capability.
The vehicle is also equipped with 360-degree cameras, adaptive cruise control, lane keeping assistance and emergency braking functions.
BMW Digital Key Plus allows compatible smartphones to be used as vehicle keys while enabling remote parking manoeuvres.
The iX3 is available in six exterior colours, all paired with the Interior Design BMW M in Black.
The colour options include Alpine White, Black Sapphire, M Brooklyn Grey and Space Silver.
Two new metallic finishes, Ocean Wave Blue and Polarised Grey, are also introduced with the latest model.
The iX3 is covered under BMW Malaysia's ownership programme, offering a five-year unlimited mileage vehicle warranty.
The package includes six years of service coverage for battery electric vehicles, an eight-year high-voltage battery warranty and 24-hour roadside assistance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Looking past statistics on the retrenchment narrative
Article:
LETTERS: A RECENT opinion piece warned that Malaysia's retrenchment wave has reached alarming, near-pandemic proportions, and that the government's claims of a healthy labour market ring hollow.
While the underlying figures are not in dispute, the claim is built on one dataset, and however accurate it is, it can still mislead if not read against the fuller picture.
The author stated that 52,607 workers had applied for unemployment benefits under Perkeso's Employment Insurance System (EIS) as of July 16, 2026, and Kuala Lumpur and Selangor together accounted for roughly six in 10 cases.
The author calls 2026 "the second-highest wave of job losses since the Covid-19 pandemic", albeit still well short of the pandemic peak (107,000). However, when viewed against two other sources, i.e., the Department of Statistics Malaysia's (DOSM) Labour Force Survey and PERKESO's own multi-year EIS record, it suggests a labour market under real but contained stress, but far from one spiralling towards a crisis.
The problem lies in what and how the data is interpreted. EIS claims measure a flow, i.e., how many people are being let go. It must be read together with DOSM's Labour Force Survey. By doing so, a different story emerges, perhaps considerably more reassuring.
Malaysia's unemployment rate stood at three per cent in May 2026, below the pre-pandemic 2019 average of 3.3 per cent, and near an 11-year low. The number of unemployed persons in 2025 (507,200) was actually lower than in 2019 (508,200), despite a labour force that has grown by nearly two million people over the same period.
The increase in EIS claims is occurring alongside a flat-to-falling unemployment rate, thus leading us to conclude that the majority of retrenched workers are finding new jobs quickly. With advertised vacancies three times higher (605,168) than active job seekers (188,062) in the first half of 2026, the labour market appears to be robust enough to absorb those being laid off.
Sceptics might ask whether 2026's aggregate numbers simply mean the reckoning is delayed, the way it eventually arrived in 2020. The two episodes look nothing alike.
In 2020, unemployment leapt from 3.5 to 5.1 per cent in a single quarter, total employment fell by roughly 359,000 workers in three months, and time-related underemployment nearly doubled (413,500 for Q2 2020 compared with 204.5 in Q2 2019) as employers cut hours rather than let staff go.
Crucially, online job vacancies collapsed to just 49,372 in the first quarter of 2020 before slowly recovering, thereby limiting the escape route for retrenched workers.  Clearly, 2026 cannot be compared with 2020. None of this should be read as downplaying the issue, but careful consideration of all the facts is important.
The opinion piece calls for action on four fronts: targeted wage subsidies for firms hiring fresh graduates, retrenched workers and long-term job seekers into permanent roles; tax incentives for SMEs prioritising local hiring alongside a review of foreign-labour dependency; closer industry-government coordination on upskilling; and transparent, published outcomes for job placement programmes and career fairs.
The government has already undertaken some actions that overlap with parts of the prescription. On May 1, 2026, the government introduced the RM710 million Progressive Acceleration for Capability and Employment (PACE) Economic Resilience Package.
Of this, RM580 million channelled through Perkeso is retrenchment-specific, targeting over 56,000 displaced workers with financial aid, job placement and re-employment interventions. The remainder, delivered through HRD Corp, PTPK and TalentCorp, funds broader employability and skills initiatives for youth, gig workers and SMEs rather than retrenched workers specifically.
This will be complemented by the Employment Insurance System (Amendment) Act 2025, passed by both houses of Parliament on June 30, 2026 but still awaiting royal assent, gazettement and a commencement date. The Act is expected to introduce a new mobility assistance allowance of RM1,000, raise the re-employment allowance rate from 25 to 50 per cent, and lift the training allowance to as much as RM30 a day.
The measures already in train – PACE, and the enhanced EIS Act once it comes into force – go some way toward answering the concerns raised. Whether they go far enough will depend on execution, and on the private sector's willingness to hire and retain, not just government's willingness to fund.
DR PETER BRIAN M. WANG
Deputy Head,
Centre of Economics and Public
Finance,
National Institute of Public
Administration (INTAN)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi backs U Mobile's innovation hub for enterprises
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has called on businesses to leverage U Mobile's Enterprise Innovation Platform Hub to strengthen cybersecurity and responsible artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.
He said the hub showcases the practical applications of 5G-Advanced technology across industries, including healthcare, agriculture and retail.
Fahmi said the technologies demonstrated could help ease nurses' workload in hospital wards, improve productivity at oil palm plantations, and enable retailers to manage inventory more efficiently while analysing customer traffic patterns.
"I see tremendous potential," he told reporters after launching the hub today.
"These technologies can help reduce the workload of nurses, improve productivity in plantations and enable the retail sector to manage stock more effectively and identify more popular customer routes based on the available data."
Fahmi also highlighted a drone-based monitoring system designed for deployment in remote areas.
He said 5G connectivity could enable drones to be used for surveillance, including along Malaysia's borders.
"I will ask the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency, the Royal Malaysia Police and several other agencies to assess the suitability of adopting this technology for border security and monitoring," he said.
He added that the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission is ready to support the initiative by ensuring reliable internet connectivity, particularly in underserved and border areas.
"I will also follow up with the Home Affairs Ministry to explore how this technology can be utilised," he said.
Earlier in his speech, Fahmi said trust, security and resilience must evolve alongside innovation as digital technologies become increasingly embedded across the economy.
He said the government remains committed to strengthening cybersecurity, enhancing network resilience and promoting the responsible and ethical adoption of AI to ensure sustainable and inclusive digital progress.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BMW defends EV investment record in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BMW Group Malaysia has defended its contribution to the country's electric vehicle (EV) ecosystem, saying its investments extend well beyond charging infrastructure to include talent development and technical capabilities.
The response comes after the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry said some automakers had not invested sufficiently in charging infrastructure despite receiving EV-related incentives.
"We believe we have contributed for more than 20 years and continue to invest across the entire ecosystem. EV transformation and charging is one topic," said BMW Group Malaysia managing director Benjamin Nagel after launching a new BMW model here today.
Nagel said the German automaker has focused on building long-term capabilities, highlighting its regional training centre in Cyberjaya.
The facility trains technicians from about 20 markets across the region and was the first BMW training centre outside the company's headquarters to receive its highest high-voltage certification.
Nagel said BMW would continue collaborating with the Selangor government and the Selangor Technical Skills Development Centre to equip technicians with expertise in both internal combustion engine and electric vehicles.
"We train Malaysians to become world-class technicians to service the cars. Transformation goes far beyond pure charging," he said.
He added that BMW would continue engaging policymakers to support the country's EV transition.
"We continue to engage with the government and find the best ways forward. Making the process easy to adapt always helps transform the market," Nagel said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BMW Malaysia urges balanced EV infrastructure push
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BMW Group Malaysia calls for a balanced approach in expanding the country's electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure without placing unnecessary pressure on automakers.
The company cautioned that any new measures should support EV growth without creating additional burdens for automakers.
Managing director Benjamin Nagel said policy proposals should be discussed with industry players before deciding on the most effective measures to support Malaysia's EV transition.
"The government comes up with ideas. I think that's important. It should be shared and discussed with the industry and then we should come with the right measures on how to continue in this transformation process.
"Make the process easy. Make the applications and to get everything done as easy as possible and maybe also encourage
the industry to really go that way," he told reporters after launching the Neue Klasse EV BMW iX3 50 xDrive M Sport Pro today.
The government is currently studying the introduction of an EV levy to help finance public charging network expansion amid concerns over infrastructure growth despite previous EV incentives.
The prospect has sparked discussions among policymakers and industry players on the best way to fund charging facilities and encourage wider EV adoption.
While describing charging infrastructure as crucial to EV adoption, Nagel said the focus should extend beyond introducing additional levies or regulations.
He said broader infrastructure readiness including sufficient electricity supply at suitable locations, was also essential for successful charging network expansion.
"The power supply needs to be there where an original equipment manufacturer can only do the end part. It cannot lay cables in the entire city.
"It is a combination and we need to find the right measures and not put additional burden on the industry.
"We should also look into it, not just bring more levies and rules but maybe also how we can improve processes and make it easier to roll this out," added Nagel.
On whether an EV levy could slow adoption, he said charging availability remained key to sustaining market growth.
"We need to continue transforming the market and charging is very crucial. It is a little bit of a chicken-and-egg situation.
"If you don't have enough chargers, at one point people will not buy EV cars as well," he said.
Nagel said BMW Malaysia has contributed to the country's charging ecosystem through collaborations with charging operators and its dealer network.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perkeso 24-hour protection claims surge more than threefold in July [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Claims under the Social Security Organisation's (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam scheme more than tripled in July, underscoring growing demand for round-the-clock social protection beyond working hours.
Perkeso said claims jumped to 2,135 in July from 616 in the previous month, reflecting the relevance of the scheme, which extends coverage for work contributors outside official working hours.
Between July 1 and July 31, Perkeso approved benefit payments for more than 90 per cent of claims within an overall processing period of less than five days.
A total of RM3.45 million was disbursed to 2,508 beneficiaries.
The payments covered medical expense reimbursement, temporary disablement benefits, funeral benefits, dependants' benefits, rehabilitation equipment and implants, as well as other forms of assistance.
Rehabilitation equipment and implants accounted for the largest share of payouts at more than RM2.5 million, aimed at easing contributors' medical expenses and enabling timely implant surgeries.
Meanwhile, more than RM842,564 was paid under temporary disablement benefits to replace lost income and support contributors and their families during medical leave.
For the period from June 1 to July 31, 2026, Perkeso received 2,751 claims under the Lindung 24 Jam scheme, averaging 45 claims a day.
Cumulative benefit payments during the first two months of the scheme reached RM4.69 million, including about RM3.69 million for rehabilitation equipment and implants and more than RM909,800 in temporary disablement benefits.
The figure excludes long-term benefits paid to beneficiaries' next of kin, which exceeded RM2 million.
Perkeso said the data demonstrated that broader social protection enables more workers to access financial assistance following accidents, reducing the need to rely on personal savings during times of hardship.
Although participation in the Lindung 24 Jam scheme remains voluntary for local workers, Perkeso urged contributors to maintain the coverage amid rising concerns over accidents occurring outside working hours.
"The sharp increase in Lindung 24 Jam benefit claims highlights the need for comprehensive social protection regardless of when or where an accident occurs.
"The scheme ensures contributors and their families are not left to shoulder the financial burden alone while providing access to rehabilitation support to help them return to work," it said.
Perkeso added that it would continue to strengthen service delivery by ensuring claims are processed swiftly and assistance reaches beneficiaries as quickly as possible.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Police expand AI, drones in border security push
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are stepping up the use of drones, artificial intelligence (AI) and cross-border intelligence sharing as part of efforts to combat smuggling and strengthen security along Malaysia's land and maritime borders.
Federal Internal Security and Public Order Department director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the move was among strategies discussed during the Thailand-Malaysia High Level Committee meeting involving the armed forces and police from both countries recently.
"The meeting has agreed to further strengthen bilateral cooperation through joint working groups, coordinated operations, regular joint patrols and enhanced intelligence sharing to tackle smuggling activities along the Malaysia-Thailand border," he told reporters at the General Operations Force Central Brigade Headquarters here today.
He said similar cooperation was also being carried out with Indonesian authorities along the Malaysia-Indonesia border.
"We want to reduce dependence on manual methods. Our focus now is on technology.
"We are using drones, enhancing intelligence sharing and looking at expanding technological capabilities, including AI, to strengthen border surveillance and enforcement," he said.
Yusri said such measures were crucial given the vast border areas stretching from Perlis to Kelantan, as well as extensive land and maritime boundaries in Sabah and Sarawak.
"The GOF currently operates 178 border posts nationwide, including 30 in Sabah, where personnel are rotated every 11 months.
"Apart from working closely with the Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom), officers stationed at the border also conduct community policing programmes to build trust and closer ties with local communities," he said.
Yusri said information received from border communities had contributed to successful enforcement operations against illegal immigrants and the smuggling of controlled goods, including petrol, diesel, rice, flour and cooking gas.
He said intelligence-led enforcement remained the cornerstone of the department's operations, with officers working alongside enforcement agencies at both federal and state levels.
"We will continue strengthening operational capabilities, expanding strategic cooperation domestically and internationally, and increasing the use of intelligence and technology to ensure our borders, territorial waters and national interests remain protected," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Abdul El-Sayed: Michigan doctor who wants to lead the left to the US Senate
Article:
THE left-wing Democratic upstart set to contest a critical US Senate seat in November's mid-term elections is a charismatic 41-year-old who once said he would have been a cab driver in Egypt but for an "accident of history."
Abdul El-Sayed on Wednesday sealed the Democratic Party's nomination to run for a seat representing the state of Michigan in the US Senate, beating out centrist candidate Haley Stevens who was backed by the party's top brass.
The charismatic, former local government health official also has his eye on a bigger prize: to lead the fight for the left in Washington against President Donald Trump.
It marks a dramatic political rise for El-Sayed, who was born in Detroit to an Egyptian father and an American mother.
"But for an accident of history that allows my dad to immigrate to Detroit to go to Wayne State University, I was supposed to be a cab driver in Egypt, like my cousins," he said after his narrow primary election victory.
"I got to go to amazing public schools, an incredible public university. I got my medical education paid for," he added. "That's what America gave me."
El-Sayed, who is a trained epidemiologist, had a prestigious academic career. He is a graduate of the University of Michigan and Columbia University in New York who also studied at Oxford on the highly regarded Rhodes Scholarship.
He subsequently became the director of public health services for Wayne County, which includes Detroit.
Muscle-bound and an eloquent speaker, El-Sayed proved a deft operator in a primary campaign that was a window into the war within the Democratic party between the moderate establishment and those further left, like veteran Senator Bernie Sanders.
The 84-year-old Independent helped campaign for El-Sayed and 31-year-old New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
In November, El-Sayed faces a tough battle to beat the Republican nominee, Mike Rogers, a former congressman who has Trump's endorsement.
[[nid:1505248]]
While both Michigan senators are currently Democrats, it is seen as a swing state.
Trump won the traditionally blue-collar, auto-manufacturing state in the 2024 presidential election.
To win, El-Sayed is counting on mobilising a progressive base, outraged by Trump's second term, and targeting bread-and-butter issues of importance across the political divide.
El-Sayed, who supports universal health care, declared his intention "to get money out of politics, put money in your pocket, pass Medicare for all."
Faced with this left-wing platform, Republicans have labelled him a dangerous extremist, while emphasising his Arab and Muslim identity.
El-Sayed has been a strong critic of Israel. AIPAC, an organisation that works to elect pro-Israel Democratic and Republican candidates, donated US$30 million to his primary election rival Stevens.
After the primary results were announced Wednesday, Trump mocked the victory of the man he called "a Communist loser who hates Jews and Israel" as "great news for the Republican Party."
Other Republicans followed suit. Its Senate caucus claimed "an alliance of communists and Islamists is taking control of the Democrat Party."
"He's actually a jihadist sympathiser," said Republican Senator Katie Britt. "They're infiltrating us from within."
It is a line of attack likely to predominate in the mid-terms, where Republicans hope to hold onto their current control of both houses of Congress.
El-Sayed seems set to give as good as he gets. On Wednesday he denounced the "bitter" campaign launched by "Mike Rogers, Donald Trump, and their MAGA allies."
He made fun of the fact that his opponents were using his full name, Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, as a scare tactic.
"Mike, listen, man," he said, referring to Rogers, his Republican rival in November's election.
"If you can't say the name...keep the name out your damn mouth. I'll be happy to give you lessons."
* The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Police seize RM15.5m worth of vapes, contraband cigarettes in Selangor raids
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have seized contraband cigarettes and vape products worth more than RM15.5 million in two major operations targeting smuggling syndicates in Selangor late last month.
Federal Internal Security and Public Order Department director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the seizures were made under Op Taring Alpha 1 and Op Taring Alpha 3.
The operations were carried out by the Wildlife Crime Bureau (WCB) and Special Investigation Intelligence Division, in collaboration with enforcement agencies including the domestic trade and cost of living ministry (KPDN) and the Gombak District Health Office.
"Op Taring Alpha 3, conducted on July 28, targeted a premises in Batu Caves believed to have been used to store and distribute vape products.
"The raid led to five people being inspected and the seizure of 131,036 boxes of vape products, 4,900 bottles of vape liquid and 25,510 electronic smoking devices of various brands," he told reporters at the General Operations Force Central Brigade headquarters here today.
Yusri said investigations found the seized products were believed to have breached provisions under the Trade Descriptions (Certification and Marking of Electronic Smoking Devices) Order, the Trade Descriptions Act and the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act.
He said the five people, along with the seized items, were handed over to KPDN and the Gombak District Health Office for further action under their respective jurisdictions.
In a separate operation under Op Taring Alpha 1 on July 27, police raided a premises in Puchong believed to have been used to store, sell and distribute duty-unpaid cigarettes.
"Three local men believed to be responsible for managing the syndicate's storage and operational activities were arrested," he said.
The raid resulted in the seizure of 166 master cases containing 8,300 cartons, or 1.66 million sticks, of JDB-brand contraband cigarettes.
The case is being investigated under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967.
Yusri said between Jan 1 and July 31 this year, WCB and the division recorded 11 vape-related cases involving five arrests and seizures worth RM9.5 million.
During the same period, he said, five contraband cigarette cases resulted in 10 arrests and seizures valued at RM6.1 million.
"Overall, WCB and the division recorded 236 cases, 411 arrests and seizures worth RM280.4 million through various operations targeting contraband, cross-border crimes, wildlife exploitation and environmental offences," he said.
Yusri attributed the success to intelligence-led enforcement and strategic cooperation with agencies including the Customs Department, KPDN, Health Ministry, Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan), Forestry Department, Fisheries Department, Veterinary Services Department and local authorities.
He said police would not compromise with those involved in smuggling activities, whether they were masterminds, suppliers, transporters, storekeepers or distributors.
"Our focus is not merely on making seizures and arrests, but on identifying, tracking and dismantling the entire syndicate, including those at the top of the network through intelligence, investigations and integrated enforcement," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: I-Berhad's first half profit rises on recurring income, AI strategy growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: I-Berhad posted a higher pre-tax profit (PBT) for the first half of its 2026 (1H FY26) financial year, supported by stronger contributions from its property development and investment businesses, as it presses ahead with its artificial intelligence (AI)-driven urban development strategy.
The company reported a PBT of RM27 million for the six months ended June 30, up from the corresponding period a year earlier despite a softer property market and more cautious consumer spending.
PBT from its property development division rose 17 per cent to RM12.1 million, driven by improved margins from its Twenty8 and 8 Premier projects.
Its property investment segment remained the company's largest recurring earnings contributor, with PBT rising 29 per cent to RM13 million, supported by about 96 per cent occupancy at Mercu Maybank Corporate Tower, full occupancy at its Block M data centre and resilient contributions from Central i-City Mall.
The company said 2026 marks a key milestone in its transformation from a traditional property developer into an integrated AI-enabled urban ecosystem, anchored by its AI Living and AI World initiatives.
It recently showcased the AI Living concept at DATUM 2026, where it demonstrated how AI, robotics and intelligent building systems can be integrated into residential developments to enhance convenience, wellness and community living.
The presentation also demonstrated the progress of the AI Living ecosystem being developed by i-City together with technology partners covering AI orchestration, robotics, wellness, building automation and digital services.
I-Berhad chairman Tan Sri Lim Kim Hong said the company's strategy is centred on creating a diversified earnings base by combining recurring investment income with AI-enabled developments.
"Our strategy is no longer simply about developing properties. We are building an integrated urban ecosystem where recurring investment income, destination businesses and AI-enabled developments reinforce one another. AI Living represents the next evolution of i-City and positions the Group to participate in the emerging convergence of property, artificial intelligence and robotics," he said.
[[nid:1505268]]
Looking ahead, I-Berhad said its long-term growth will be underpinned by about RM5 billion in remaining gross development value within i-City. Upcoming AI World projects, including AI Living residences, are expected to drive future earnings while complementing its expanding portfolio of recurring income assets.
Lim said the company's diversified business model, growing recurring income stream and AI-led development strategy position it for sustainable long-term growth despite near-term market uncertainties.
While near-term market conditions remain selective, I-Berhad remains confident that its diversified earnings base, growing recurring income and AI-driven development strategy provide a strong platform for sustainable long-term growth and shareholder value creation, he said.

Title: Shell approves Malikai Phase 3 to lift Sabah oil output by 60pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shell has approved the third phase of its Malikai deepwater development offshore Sabah.
This marks another investment in Malaysia's upstream sector as the energy major seeks to sustain its global liquids production over the long term.
Sabah Shell Petroleum Company, a subsidiary of Shell plc, has taken the final investment decision for the project, which will involve drilling four new production wells to increase recoverable oil volumes from the Malikai field.
The expansion is expected to raise Malikai's oil production by 60 per cent, from about 25,000 barrels per day (bpd) currently to around 40,000 bpd when Phase 3 comes on stream in the third quarter of 2028.
The project supports Shell's strategy of maintaining material liquids production at around 1.4 million bpd through 2030 and beyond, while reinforcing Malaysia's role in its deepwater portfolio.
Siti Sulaiman, country chair of Shell Malaysia and senior vice president Upstream Malaysia, said the investment underscores Shell's long-term commitment to the country.
"The final investment decision of the Malikai Phase 3 development marks another important milestone in Shell's long-standing commitment to Malaysia.
"We look forward to further contributing to the state's economic growth through investments in competitive and resilient projects," she said.
Shell said the investment reflects its continued confidence in Malaysia's deepwater potential.
Operating under the stewardship of Petronas' Malaysia Petroleum Management, the company said it remains committed to supporting the country's economic growth and energy transition through competitive and resilient upstream investments.
